name: slirp4netns
desc: User-mode networking for unprivileged network namespaces
why: A user-mode TCP/IP stack that gives unprivileged containers networking, a neat door into how network namespaces and NAT work.

brief.what_it_is: slirp4netns is a user-mode networking program for Linux network namespaces that an unprivileged user can create. You run it on the host with the PID of a process in the namespace and a TAP device name, such as tap0. It attaches that TAP device to a user-space TCP/IP stack (libslirp, the "slirp" stack), which gives the namespace outbound internet access without root. The namespace ends up with a tap0 interface (the README example shows 10.0.2.100/24) and can reach the Internet through the host. It runs as a separate process alongside the namespace rather than as a library.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says that since Linux 3.8 unprivileged users can create network and user namespaces, but those namespaces were not very useful because creating veth pairs across the host and namespace still needs root, so a namespace had no internet connection.
brief.how_it_works: slirp4netns connects a TAP device inside the target network namespace to the user-mode TCP/IP stack from libslirp. The README says it is optimized to avoid copying packets across namespaces, and it benchmarks faster than vde_plug and VPNKit on an iperf3 test from 2018. The example sets up a resolver by pointing resolv.conf at the 10.0.2.3 nameserver that slirp provides.

commands_seen.context: Terminal 1: creates user, network, and mount namespaces as an unprivileged user, the first step of the quick start.
Terminal 2: starts slirp4netns against the namespace PID saved in /tmp/pid and creates a tap0 device with the given MTU.
Run inside the namespace: writes a resolv.conf that points at the slirp DNS address 10.0.2.3.
Run inside the namespace: bind-mounts the custom resolv.conf over /etc/resolv.conf so name lookups work.
Run inside the namespace as a final check that outbound internet access works.
Prints the slirp4netns version and the linked libslirp version, shown in the maintenance section.
Example of installing the distribution package on Debian or Ubuntu.

commands_seen.cmd: sudo apt-get install libglib2.0-dev libslirp-dev libcap-dev libseccomp-dev
commands_seen.context: Build dependencies for compiling from source on apt-based systems.
First step of the source build, run from the repository root.
Configures the source build with /usr as the install prefix, before make and make install.

brief.install_notes: Static binaries for x86_64, aarch64, armv7l, s390x, ppc64le, and riscv64 are on the GitHub releases page, and packages exist for RHEL/CentOS, Fedora, Arch, openSUSE, SUSE, Debian, Ubuntu, NixOS, Gentoo, Slackware, Void, and Alpine. If unshare fails, the README says some distros (Debian, Arch, old CentOS 7) may need sysctl changes: set user.max_user_namespaces=28633 and, where present, kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1, then run sudo sysctl --system. Building from source needs libglib, libslirp (v4.1.0 or later), libcap, and libseccomp development packages. For a static build, configure with LDFLAGS=-static. If --prefix is set to $HOME, make install does not need sudo. No account or hardware is required.
brief.standout: It turns an unprivileged namespace, which is otherwise cut off from the network, into a working internet connection without root or veth pairs. The 'slirp' idea is decades old, but it is now the networking backend for rootless Podman, Buildah, RootlessKit, and k3s.
brief.status: maintained. The README's maintenance table lists v1.2.x as Active and older branches as End of Life, with the most recent EOL date May 2, 2022. It links to releases and security advisories. I did not check the releases page or the latest commit date, so the most recent release date is unknown.
brief.caveats: Linux only, because it depends on Linux network namespaces. The README's iperf3 benchmark is from August 2018, on RootlessKit's Travis CI, and the README does not say it has been rerun, though it mentions a regular make benchmark on CI. Before v1.0.0 the repo tracked libslirp/QEMU CVEs, and it no longer does, so the security record for libslirp sits elsewhere. The README also mentions that unshare may need kernel or sysctl changes on some distros. The GPL-2.0-or-later license is in COPYING. The manual (slirp4netns.1.md) has a Bugs section that I did not read.
quotes: slirp4netns allows connecting a network namespace to the Internet in a completely unprivileged way, by connecting a TAP device in a network namespace to the usermode TCP/IP stack ("slirp").
Starting with Linux 3.8, unprivileged users can create network_namespaces(7) along with user_namespaces(7).
slirp4netns is faster than vde_plug and VPNKit because slirp4netns is optimized to avoid copying packets across the namespaces.
